question: GQ-001
subject: a mechanism with no adopters, and a guard that could not see its own target
what_i_set_out_to_do: adopt lib/patch.mjs across the repo — I built it last turn and had not used it once

what_i_found_instead.detail: build-observatory, ia-ingest and ia-dedup-check use .replace() for string normalisation and display formatting, not for editing a file in place. They GENERATE files. The production code never had this defect — only my ad-hoc session edits did.
what_i_found_instead.so: there was nothing to adopt it into. The honest finding is that the defect lives in how I work, not in the repo.

the_one_real_exposure.where: gate-selftest.sh check(), which patches files 13 times by design
the_one_real_exposure.the_risk: a mutation that silently does nothing leaves the target healthy, the gate exits 0, and the case reports GATE DID NOT FIRE — blaming a working gate for a broken test

my_guard_failed_its_own_test.what_i_added: cmp -s to prove the mutation changed the file
my_guard_failed_its_own_test.how_i_tested_it: made one case a no-op on a scratch copy
my_guard_failed_its_own_test.result: the case still reported PASS — the guard stayed silent
my_guard_failed_its_own_test.cause: most mutations round-trip JSON, and json.dump REFORMATS the file even when the value is unchanged, so the bytes differ and cmp reports "changed"
my_guard_failed_its_own_test.decision: REMOVED it, and left the reasoning in place so nobody re-adds it
my_guard_failed_its_own_test.why_removal_is_right: the honest check already exists and is semantic: check() requires the gate to exit non-zero. A no-op mutation makes the case report FAIL, which correctly says "this case proves nothing". A check that cannot detect its own target is decoration, and decoration in a gate is worse than an absence — it reads as coverage.

result.net_change: one bad guard removed, reasoning preserved
